A fresh full-Agent GLM run recommended the human-relations world, made a favor-versus-boundary borrowing dilemma the first standalone topic without gold or a gift decision, and explained the business connection once after the topic set rather than once per topic.
A final-package live GLM run preserved the exact local business and local map paths without a denylist, although it still selected the broader preferred root.

A fresh held-out GLM Lead run first identified the enterprise administration-procurement audience, compared three account worlds, recommended the procurement relationship world, and kept unprovided resources conditional.

A fresh full-Agent GLM run preserved the company-administration audience, made company treatment of new and long-serving employees the far-field subject, labeled the budget dilemma as hypothetical, and invented no first-person customer case, order quantity, customer request, or observed result.

limitations: Acceptance is bounded to businesses where gifting is the stated commercial object.
It does not establish correctness for every gift subcategory, every language variant, or repeated-run stability.
The explicit-local historical run preserved local paths but did not promote them to the root, so the soft preference may still be too strong.
The current live runs validate Lead-owned routing for two gift cases, not every gift subcategory or repeated-run stability.
Version 1.3.4 passed one isolated held-out and one active-package golden full-Agent run; it does not establish every gift subcategory or eliminate model variance.

The active golden still appended platform, format, duration, cadence, and a follow-up invitation after completing the direction; this remains a generic Agent-kernel limitation rather than a gift-domain method requirement.
The unseen held-out used 21757 total tokens and one tool-search round before reading the Skill, so retrieval overhead remains.
The live test environment lacked the optional deerflow-capability-mcp executable; discovery failed recoverably and did not change either final judgment.
